advice: Experiment: Starting from existing-sme (SHA-256 3719c58530161598ab9a537a43be749a5287c8d8dbd35b855e5afea97cd15258), combine the transpose and GEMM helpers into one SME-targeted, locally streaming helper that performs the transpose, then GEMM, within a single streaming region. Keep the same transpose layout and work order, four ZA accumulators, selectors 0–3, FP32 arithmetic, direct stores, and general-size tail handling. Keep allocation and freeing in gemm. This removes the streaming-region boundary between the two helpers while preserving entry and exit at the internal helper boundary, within the gemm call. Hypothesis: reducing SME streaming setup and teardown may improve complete-call time. The full-call effect is unverified; no supplied measurement isolates this cost. Inspect the candidate assembly to confirm one streaming-region entry/exit and unchanged ZA behavior, then check n<=0, small sizes, odd tails, guards, and tolerance 0.002. Measure complete gemm calls with fresh repeated paired AC controls under the frozen benchmark. Do not infer a gain from instruction counts or compare against historical AC scores.
risks: Combining the helpers may increase register pressure or change compiler code generation, including spills or transpose scheduling. Streaming-region overhead may be small relative to transpose and GEMM work, and the merged code may regress. Preserve the ABI and all frozen benchmark rules; accept only if correctness passes and repeated paired measurements meet the existing gates.
